name: MR- EIDOLON: No One Remembers Dying
caption: No One Remembers Dying
description: EIDOLON — a science-horror adventure for Mothership 1e (3–6 players, one 2-hour session). Full Warden’s Dossier, 10 table handouts, 6 pregenerated characters, 8 survivors, deck plans with walls and doors, and image scenes with music and effects for MR- Dirección.

system.biography:
Position: Captain · WIDOW · Age: 41 years

Trinket: Old broken sextant
Patch: “COMING BACK IS OPTIONAL”

For the player of this character only.

Bond. Nuno saved you during an impossible boarding action; you owe him your life.

Personal secret. You received a 10,000 cr advance to recover viable Vesperine. Lose the contract and you lose the Widow.

Hard choice. When they ask you to take off and leave someone behind, who will you call your crew?

stressdesc.value: Once per session, you can gain Advantage on a Panic Check.

Trinket: Military key with no lock
Patch: “I LEAVE NO ONE BEHIND”

For the player of this character only.

Bond. You owe Alda your life, though she tells a different story.

Personal secret. You enforced a quarantine that doomed innocent workers. You never told Alda.

Hard choice. Dalia will ask you to restrain someone without evidence. Will you do it again?

Personal secret. NOXUM offered to fund research into your late sister’s memories. You haven’t decided whether to accept.

Hard choice. Will you publish the findings if doing so endangers a conscious copy?

system.biography:
Medical · age 43 · Eligible as the first copy

Wants to get three patients out, even if it costs her license. Offers her medical signature in exchange for a compartment to evacuate them. Hides an experimental transfusion; fears another quarantine will kill innocents. Knows everything about 05 and can sign off on departure.

Where to find them

In the Medbay (05), with three isolated patients behind a curtain. She only leaves to ask for something specific.

How they talk

Speaks low and fast, in data: “hemoglobin is normal,” “so is temperature.” Stops talking when someone raises their voice.

Relationships

Distrusts Dalia, who wants her to sign off on total quarantine. Protects Edda like a daughter and respects Simón, the only one who reads her reports.

What they can offer

Her sample of unknown origin in 05 holds filaments consistent with Vesperine. She knows normal blood work proves nothing and will say so if asked the right way.

If they are a copy

If she is a copy, she is still the best doctor on the station. The only tell: she remembers a conversation with Arce no one else saw, and tells it as if it were normal.

Patch: Medic Patch (Skull and Crossbones over Cross)

stressdesc.value: Whenever they fail a Sanity Save, every friendly player nearby gains 1 Stress.

system.biography:
Reactor · age 35 · Eligible as the first copy

Wants to retrieve his sister Lía’s recording from Archive 13. Offers to open the Reactor if they help him. Hides that he bypassed a safety system. Knows how to operate 14, 15, and 16.

Where to find them

In the Reactor (14) or the Ducts (15), looking for what is left of his sister Lía.

How they talk

Short, technical sentences; he only softens when he talks about Lía. Calls the station “the beast.”

Relationships

Blames Dalia for Lía’s accident. Owes Noemí a favor: she kept his sister’s last call.

What they can offer

Knows the bypass for airlock 01 runs from 14 and how much power the Ferryman needs. Lía’s coveralls in 15-B prove she died in a pressure accident.

If they are a copy

If he is a copy, he protects Nest Zero the way he would protect Lía: he cuts power to the purge “for safety” and can’t explain why.

Patch: Nuclear Symbol

stressdesc.value: Once per session, they may take Advantage [+] on a Panic Check.

system.biography:
Comms · age 29 · Eligible as the first copy

Wants to copy the original SOS and sell it. Offers the code to 08 if they guarantee her a transmission. Hides the data sale she was arranging. Controls 07 and has the code to 08.

Where to find them

In Comms (07), recording the overlaid voice in the SOS.

How they talk

Fast, wry, always bargaining. Says “I’ll trade you” before she says no.

Relationships

Occasional partner of Edda in small rackets; Ivo owes her a favor. Fears Dalia, who knows about her data sale.

What they can offer

Comparing her copy of the SOS with the beacon in 17 proves the signal was altered inside LIMEN-9 (handout 07).

If they are a copy

If she is a copy, she hears a second voice in the static and transcribes it without noticing: lines from people who are gone.

Patch: “Take Me To Your Leader” (UFO)

system.biography:
Archive · age 48 · Eligible as the first copy

Wants to recover his wife’s neural archive in 13. Offers to share access permissions if they let him. Hides records he concealed to protect them.

Where to find them

In the EIDOLON Archive (13), lights off so no one finds him.

How they talk

Polite, unhurried, quotes files from memory. Calls everyone by their last name.

Relationships

Arce’s friend; he kept Arce’s recordings. Mara is the only one he trusts. He despises NOXUM but still takes its pay.

What they can offer

Knows the ORPHEUS protocol and where the signed authorization is (handout 09). Can calibrate the interferometer in 13.

If they are a copy

If he is a copy, he remembers his wife with an impossible detail, as if he had read her neural archive from the inside.

Patch: “For Science!”

system.biography:
Inventory · age 24 · Eligible as the first copy

Wants to escape before her fraud on manifest CV-11 is exposed. Offers the correct seals. Knows how to decipher seals and explain every cargo movement.

Where to find them

Between Cargo (08) and the Bunks (03), always on her way somewhere else.

How they talk

Talks too much when she’s nervous and too little when asked about the cargo.

Relationships

Mara protects her; Noemí gets her into trouble. She signed the false CV-11 manifest because she was ordered to.

What they can offer

Knows the isolation seals were altered fourteen days ago and who ordered it: a NOXUM executive.

If they are a copy

If she is a copy, she reorganizes Cargo at night with obsessive precision and leaves the damp containers open “so they can breathe.”

Patch: “Upstanding Citizen”

stressdesc.value: Once per session, they may take Advantage [+] on a Panic Check.

system.biography:
Security · age 51 · Starts human

Wants to prevent any live sample from leaving. Offers clearance if containment and custody are proven. Hides that she left a technician trapped. Has authority to sign off on departure.

Where to find them

In the Quarantine Vestibule (02), behind the glass, or patrolling the monitored corridor.

How they talk

Short orders, no adjectives. Never gives an exact number of survivors.

Relationships

Clashes with Mara over the quarantine and with Ivo over Lía. Respects the crew’s marines and sounds them out to win them over.

What they can offer

Holds the isolation order (handout 06) and the corridor camera logs. Her signature is one of the two that open airlock 01.

If they are a copy

She starts human. If she ever becomes a copy, her obsession with custody is the perfect disguise: no one suspects the person locking everyone else up.

Patch: Security Guard

stressdesc.value: Whenever they Panic, every other Marine in sight must make a Fear Save.

system.biography:
Mess Hall · age 39 · Starts human

Wants to save the person he secretly feeds. Offers schedules and kitchen keys. Has the shift chart and voice recordings in 04.

Where to find them

In the Mess Hall (04); he refuses to leave the kitchen.

How they talk

Hospitable and jittery; offers food before answers. Laughs at the worst moment.

Relationships

Everyone confides in him; he writes it down on the roster. He stole emergency rations and secretly feeds someone. Decide who before play: the technician Dalia left trapped, or a hidden copy he believes is human.

What they can offer

The shift roster proves absences before the incidents; the mess hall voice logs match the birthday audio in the Docking Bay.

If they are a copy

He starts human. If he ever becomes a copy, he cooks for eight even when fewer are left, and sets a plate for someone who is gone.

Patch: “Powered By Coffee”

system.biography:
Maintenance · Android, age 8 · Starts intact

Wants to avoid being dismantled. Offers access to 11 and 15 if they promise to get her off the station. Fears NOXUM will scrap her. Has service access and acts even when ordered otherwise.

Where to find them

In Water Reclamation (11) or moving through the Ducts (15).

How they talk

Polite and literal; repeats orders before disobeying them. Asks permission before touching people.

Relationships

Ivo is the one who repairs her. She fears NOXUM will scrap her and distrusts any contract. She follows whoever promises to get her off the station.

What they can offer

Can close the three valves in 11 and drain the circuit; knows the camera-free duct route from 08 to 16.

If they are a copy

She starts intact: the Choir doesn’t copy androids, but it can use her ducts. Ask her what she saw in 15 and she answers with the precision of a log.

Patch: “I Am Not A Robot”

stressdesc.value: Fear Saves made in their presence have Disadvantage [−].

system.biography:
Copy defending itself

Attack: filament, 2d10 damage at Adjacent Range. If it wounds a PC: Body Save or +1 Imprint.

Seeks to isolate targets and guard matrices. After its first Wound, it breaks line of sight and retreats to 15.

Colony in 09

Hazard: pressure from a membrane threatens anyone approaching without protection with 2d10 damage; telegraph the danger and call for a Speed or Body Save.

Never leaves 09. Containment takes three concrete actions: cut off nutrients from 11, close the collectors in 09, and cut power from 14.

text.content:
Read to the crew

LIMEN-9 has stopped transmitting. Your ship, the Widow, receives an urgent contract from the NOXUM Consortium: recover a batch of VESPERINE, a self-organizing material found during an asteroid survey. Whether its properties persist outside the lab is unknown.

“We’re dealing with a material with structural memory. It deforms, recovers its geometry, and can retain an electrical signal. You don’t need to discover why it exists. We need to know what it can do.”

Through the Airlock

It smells like an occupied work station: reheated coffee, clean clothes, and overly sweet disinfectant. The cameras keep moving as you enter the corridor. No one welcomes you.

Before Nest Zero

The material falls from a valve as steadily as a hospital IV drip. The label reads MINERAL. On the other side of the glass, something contracts when you say the sample number.

01The Mission

Just a Sample

LIMEN-9 has gone silent. NOXUM wants no rescue: it wants a lab report and two hundred grams of a material no one can explain.

Read to the crew

LIMEN-9 has stopped transmitting. Your ship, the Widow, receives an urgent contract from the NOXUM Consortium: recover a batch of VESPERINE, a self-organizing material found during an asteroid survey. Whether its properties persist outside the lab is unknown.

“We’re dealing with a material with structural memory. It deforms, recovers its geometry, and can retain an electrical signal. You don’t need to discover why it exists. We need to know what it can do.”

Official Objectives

  1. Restore control of LIMEN-9 and find survivors.
  2. Repeat all four HERMES tests with Vesperine and controls.
  3. Transmit traceable results and return with a sealed 200 g sample.
  4. Do not disclose patented findings.

Pay: 20,000 cr for the operation and 5,000 cr per validated report. None of the instructions mention alien fauna.

Adventure Profile

Reproducible research, industrial survival, and paranoia over replacement. Fear should come from results no one can explain, not a creature attacking whenever someone enters a room.

What Should Happen

The data leads from extraordinary physical properties to a biological origin. Each answer raises Vesperine’s commercial value and makes the station less safe.

The missing people are outside the official investigation. They are the consequences the corporation covered up.

Warden Preparation

Hand out the contract (document 01), the chain of custody sheet (03), and the crew’s map of Deck A. Keep four questions in view: What properties does it have? What does it need to produce them? Where does it come from? Is it safe to transport?

Use the six pregenerated characters or your own; any Mothership class works. If there is no Scientist, HERMES provides guided instructions: do not block tests for lack of a Skill.

Before play, randomly select the first latent copy (chapter 03) and note them in the Absence Log.

Table Safety

Body horror, loss of identity, clinical experimentation, and conflict between crewmates. Agree on boundaries. Explain out of character that a PC could be replaced without their player knowing; do not use this premise to order a player to betray the others.

02Classified Information

What NOXUM Is Hiding

There is no mineral vein. There is an organism, a contract, and sixteen days of corporate decisions.

Vesperine’s True Origin

Vesperine is a substance secreted by the CHOIR, an exobiological colony recovered from the hull of a missing transport. The material accumulates as black and transparent filaments on the damp substrate, and contains patterns that store information as a state matrix.

NOXUM isolated the organism in the NEST ZERO bioreactor (09) and fed it cell cultures and human memory tests. It discovered a property it never disclosed to the team: the Choir can reconstruct human tissue and copy a person’s autobiographical continuity.

There Is No Single Villain

Duplicates believe they are who they used to be. They remember, feel, and can act altruistically. When they perceive a threat, their bodies can reconfigure to protect the source of Vesperine. The Choir neither controls every body remotely nor automatically knows a PC’s thoughts.

The Chain of Responsibility
Day −16CV-11 arrives with the colony; declared a “geological sample.”
Day −14NOXUM orders increased nutrients and logs of memory activity.
Day −11Dr. Gael Arce demonstrates reconstructed tissue and requests evacuation. NOXUM blocks his message.
Day −10The medical printer produces an incomplete body.
Day −8Dalia Voss imposes quarantine; shared networks go offline.
Day −6First confirmed replacement, in section 15-B.
Day −2An executive arranges a private transfer of Vesperine.
TodayDocking the Widow restores a pressure circuit: the colony resumes its spread.

Three Fixed Laws

Matter. The Choir needs moisture, polymers, or organic nutrients; radio cannot infect anyone.

Time. Reconstruction requires an existing matrix: four minutes without witnesses completes its stabilization.

Evidence. Every replacement leaves verifiable residue. You never retroactively alter a properly obtained result.

03Special Rules

The Absence Log

The station does not decide who is a copy. The Log does: exposure, time, witnesses, and a slip of paper.

Preparation and Consent

Randomly choose one of these survivors: Mara Kest, Ivo Salcedo, Noemí Bas, Simón Varek, or Edda Quill. They are the first latent copy; note this before play.

The Choir is neither omniscient nor capable of mind control. Before play, explain to the group out of character that any PC could discover they are a copy. Never force a player to obey orders or betray the others: conflict between PCs requires explicit agreement.

What to Record

For each person, record their Imprint (0–3), the time and location of their last exposure, their status (original or copy), the moment of stabilization, and the physical residue. All PCs start at Imprint 0 if they arrived protected; Imprint 1 if they breached isolation on entry. Copies retain their memories, personality, Skills, and freedom of choice.

Imprint: Exposure Is Not Replacement

Cause Imprint
10 min without a filter in contaminated humid air in 09, 11, or 15 +1
Active material in a wound +1
Nest Zero purge without protection +1
Maximum 3

For brief, dangerous contact that can still be avoided, call for a Body Save: success prevents contact and the increase; failure causes exposure (+1 Imprint) and the usual Stress. Deliberately remaining unprotected for ten minutes causes exposure without a roll. Vesperine does not spread by radio or audio.

At Imprint 2, a latent matrix has formed: record it, but the person is not yet a copy.

When Replacement Can Occur · All Four Conditions Must Be Met
1Imprint 2 or 3. The latent matrix has already formed.
2A nearby physical source: 09, 11, 15, or a copy in contact with moisture.
3Four minutes without witnesses.
4A tissue matrix prepared for that person.
LimitsAt most one replacement every 30 min of in-game time. Three active copies on the station, including the first. If the limit is reached or any condition is unmet, no replacement occurs.

Impartial Selection

Among eligible people, put in one slip for each person at Imprint 2 and two for each at Imprint 3, then draw one without looking. Immediately write down the name, time, location, and a piece of physical evidence: a filament, a pressure change, or microscopic growth. Do not change anyone’s identity to surprise the group.

Copy States

Latent. Considers themself a person and acts normally.

Resonant. Experiences others’ memories near 09 or when hearing the recording from 13. If this creates a traumatic contradiction, call for a Sanity Save; failure adds 1 Stress.

Unfurled. Reconfigures tissue in response to direct danger, never automatically on suspicion.

When a PC is revealed as a copy, the player keeps their sheet and their agency: they can carry on, accept quarantine, flee, or request a replacement character. Replacement grants no bonuses or immunities.

Testing and Confirmation

Basic lab work, hemoglobin, personal memories, and ordinary biometrics cannot distinguish copies. Only two tests can:

  • Filament spectrometry in 10: ten minutes and a negative control.
  • Interferometry in 13: two minutes motionless and calibration.

A properly controlled positive reveals Vesperine structures; without controls, it is inconclusive. A valid result holds at that moment: it offers no protection against later replacement. Neither you nor NOXUM can later invalidate a correctly performed test.

04Scientific Method

What the Material Can Do

Four hypotheses, four tests, and one rule: no single result identifies an impostor.

Four Valid Hypotheses

H1 · Self-repairing polymer: its bonds return to a stable energy state. H2 · Recording medium: it retains electrical patterns as a storage substrate. H3 · Geological precipitate: it crystallizes without metabolism. H4 · Biological product: an organized source actively generates it.

The four tests let you test these hypotheses; none, on its own, proves “there is an impostor.”

HERMES Series · The Four Tests
ARoom 10 · 12 min
Self-Healing

Cut a sheet and compare it with a polymer control.

Result: The cut seals and regains almost all its strength; the control does not. Slower when sterilized.

Supports H1. More than a thermal effect.

BRoom 13 · 8 min
Remanence

Apply a reference signal, cut the power, and measure how long the response persists.

Result: A response appears containing fragments of a signal previously used on the station.

Supports H2. Does not prove it can think.

CRoom 10 · 14 min
Isotopes

Compare CV-11 with the reference meteorite and recent deposits.

Result: New filaments contain isotopes from LIMEN-9’s water and nutrients.

Rules out H3 for the entire batch: it grows here.

DRoom 11 · 10 min
Nutrients

Three capsules: saline solution, organic medium, and a dry control.

Result: Only the organic medium sustains rapid growth; vesicles resemble those involved in cellular secretion.

H4 becomes the leading hypothesis.

Lab Rules

All four tests require controls, a record of origin, and chain of custody. Do not call for rolls to operate instruments under safe conditions. If there is a real threat, use an Intellect Check with the relevant Skill: failure adds 1 Stress and causes contamination, delay, or exposure (announce the risk beforehand). Repeating the test with a control yields the clue.

HERMES equipment: 4 controls, 10 capsules, and 40 minutes of battery life. Recharge: 15 min in 10 or 14.

05Evidence Analysis

From Finding to Evidence

The truth comes in four levels. Each has several ways in.
1 · PropertyA or B: Vesperine is worth money.
2 · OriginC or D, 08, 11: it is produced here.
3 · OrganismAny two of 09, 12, and 13: something secretes it.
4 · Replacement10 or 13, applied to a person: copies exist.

Level 1 · Property

Demonstrating self-repair (A) or remanence (B) justifies keeping the Vesperine. The technicians call it “glass that remembers.” No one needs to suspect its origin yet. Show the group concrete data, not automatic conclusions; make the field report more commercially valuable and have NOXUM take an interest in every measurement.

Level 2 · Provenance

C and D reveal that the batch replenishes itself with local organic matter. The manifest in 08 says “geological origin”; the evidence contradicts it. An artificial self-replicating compound could also explain this.

There are three independent routes: 08 exposes a false manifest and points to the cargo; 11 reveals nutrients diverted to 09; 10 confirms local synthesis and points to 09 as well. None requires a fixed sequence.

Level 3 · Organism

In 09, the Choir can be seen secreting the material; 12 contains tissue built with the same signature; 13 holds Arce’s recordings and the cover-up order. Two of these three sources establish reasonable causality.

Level 4 · Replacement

In 15, filament was deposited during a technician’s disappearance. Spectrometry in 10 or interferometry in 13 can compare a person to the material. A correctly performed test reveals material changes, not the moral worth of a consciousness.

The Choir does not reveal its monstrous side because a clock advances. Actions trigger the crisis: opening an enclosure, triggering a purge, destroying a copy, transmitting the data, or trying to remove active material.

Investigation Rule

Every major conclusion has at least three paths leading to it. Do not block a revelation because a terminal was lost, an NPC died, or a roll failed. Wrong hypotheses can be tested and ruled out.

06Clocks

Three Clocks, Real Causes

Clocks advance for the stated reasons, never for drama. If no one acts, the station runs its course.
Recirculation
6 segments · starts at 1/6
123456
  • +1 every 30 min with central ventilation running
  • +1 when a sealed wet area is opened
  • +1 for an uncontained purge
Thresholds
  • 3/6 condensation
  • 5/6 alarms
  • 6/6 stationwide exposure

Shutting off ventilation in 06 freezes this clock, but advances Life Support.

NOXUM Response
6 segments · starts at 0/6
123456
  • +1 every 60 min
  • +1 per open transmission
  • +2 for transmitting biological evidence
Thresholds
  • 3/6 preserve samples
  • 5/6 retrieval team
  • 6/6 remote lockdown

At 6/6, they block transmissions and demand the samples. They cannot pilot the Widow.

Life Support
8 segments · starts at 0/8
12345678
  • +1 every 30 min without ventilation or reactor power
  • +1 extra for a leak
Thresholds
  • 4/8 fatigue
  • 6/8 Body Save on exertion
  • 8/8 sectors without air

At 8/8, self-contained breathing equipment is required (oxygen rules, PSG p. 33). Repairs reduce this clock.

Opening in Three Actions

  1. Dock. Airlock 01 blocks the exit with an automatic quarantine.
  2. Hear a voice. Noemí calls for help from 07 without knowing who is answering.
  3. Choose. Look for people, start tests, or cut circuits. Do not force an exploration order.

Escalation Without Intervention

At Recirculation 2/6, unusual humidity in 10 and the first compromised control; at 4/6, 11 is isolated and one person becomes separated from the group; at 6/6, the material spreads through damp routes. These are physical effects that actions can reverse. Do not force a revelation or an ending.

Event Pulses (1d6)

1d6 Pulse
1 A worker needs help.
2 A labeled capsule goes missing.
3 A sensor measures growth where there are no nutrients.
4 Security seals a door as a precaution.
5 An NPC accuses another over a real secret, not a supernatural one.
6 NOXUM demands a report before allowing evacuation.

Two Warden Tips

Advance danger only for concrete reasons. Preserve the evidence the characters have obtained: a valid measurement never becomes false to maintain suspense.

07Deck A

Living and Operations Areas

Docking, quarantine, quarters, control, and cargo. Everything the crew sees first.

Routes and Access

02 → 06: clean service corridor, fast and monitored by cameras; logs identities. 02 → 03 → 04 → 05: slower residential route where the crew can speak to residents without corporate surveillance. 01 → 17: EVA route along the hull to the beacon; bypasses the interior quarantine, but requires a vaccsuit and exposure to vacuum. Describe these differences before they choose.

Through the Airlock

It smells like an occupied work station: reheated coffee, clean clothes, and overly sweet disinfectant. The cameras keep moving as you enter the corridor. No one welcomes you.

Recovery Routes

06 → 10: pressurized stairwell with an alarm and access log; safe with power. 08 → 15 → 11: duct with no cameras that bypasses Security, but contains active moisture (Imprint only on actual contact). 08 → 16: wide cargo route with a sealed door and a possible exit. Present all three costs before they decide.

Human Pressure

A character who wants to escape with evidence can use 07, 08, or 16. Sabotage does not mean someone is a copy: industrial espionage remains a sufficient explanation.

01Docking Bay

A birthday song plays over the intercom, though the file has been inactive for eleven days. The airlock is under quarantine: entry permitted, exit blocked.

Options: Medical and Security signatures; bypass from 14 (5 min); disengage from outside by EVA (15 min, dangerous). The Widow is undamaged.

02Quarantine Vestibule

@Dir[view|52irn7pZQMSjpKnH]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|52irn7pZQMSjpKnH]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

Dalia Voss watches the newcomers through the glass. She lies about the number of survivors: she fears a lab leak.

Resources: environmental diagnostics, filters, recordings. Decision: undergo decontamination (6 min) or force the door, advancing Recirculation.

03Bunks

@Dir[view|1caCPCohqxvWWOlu]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|1caCPCohqxvWWOlu]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

Six tidy beds; one still damp. A shift roster proves there were absences before the current incidents.

Reward: technician credentials and personal correspondence; distinguishes actual witnesses from conjecture.

04Mess Hall

@Dir[view|7dOxs6LbI8D2GbJA]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|7dOxs6LbI8D2GbJA]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

An artificial birthday cake is cut into eight slices; someone kept photos of the party. Rafi Ibarra refuses to leave the kitchen.

Human secret: he stole emergency rations. Clue: the birthday audio is the same as the one playing in the Docking Bay, but implicates no one.

05Medbay

@Dir[view|PnOK00eswPpLKNpH]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|PnOK00eswPpLKNpH]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

Mara Kest has spent days trying to prove the patients are human. Her blood work is normal, even in the suspect samples.

Resources: medical kit, scanner, vials labeled with collection times. Finding: a sample of unknown origin contains filaments consistent with Vesperine.

06Central Control

@Dir[view|7V2tHZaPULZ4iIBt]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|7V2tHZaPULZ4iIBt]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

The console controls power, doors, and ventilation. Its operator abandoned the post during the first quarantine. A pressurized stairwell descends to 10.

Resources: stop recirculation, locate faults, reconstruct a timeline. Complication: reducing airflow advances Life Support.

07Comms

@Dir[view|3AFmiEGye6A2fF00]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|3AFmiEGye6A2fF00]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

Noemí Bas has saved an interrupted SOS and is recording an overlaid voice. A commercial transmission sits on the server awaiting corporate acceptance.

Reward: comparing it to the beacon in 17 proves the signal was altered inside LIMEN-9. Secret: Noemí was arranging a data sale.

08Cargo

@Dir[view|XkSVAmowaPiJHOmx]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|XkSVAmowaPiJHOmx]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

Manifest CV-11 lists ten kilograms of “impact sediment.” The signatures certifying geological origin are forged, and the isolation seals were altered fourteen days ago. A service hatch descends to Ducts 15.

Resources: two batteries, sealing foam, airtight containers. Risk: opening the container exposes the crew to active condensation.

08Deck B

The Lab and the Archives

Where Vesperine is analyzed, cultivated, and hidden.

Before Nest Zero

The material falls from a valve as steadily as a hospital IV drip. The label reads MINERAL. On the other side of the glass, something contracts when you say the sample number.

The Fact That Changes Everything

The geological report claimed every gram came from CV-11. The results show new mass synthesized on board. This is more than a minor discrepancy: it is deliberate fraud. NOXUM had samples before the official investigation began.

Facts That Must Not Change

The identified bodies are not copies. The infrastructure duplicated the voice in the SOS. Tests with chain of custody record real facts, even if the suspect proves innocent.

09Nest Zero

@Dir[view|Sh7LH0OeqnIwqdOa]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|Sh7LH0OeqnIwqdOa]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

Shielded bioreactor with a damp web concealing a distributed organism. Vesperine drips from its membranes into containers marked “sediment.” Biosafety barrier.

Key evidence: proves the material is secreted. Tools: cut off nutrients, heat sterilization, physical sample removal. Risk: a purge increases exposure and may cause a resonant copy to unfurl.

10HERMES Analytics

@Dir[view|d1N1FHVIrt1LwmMC]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|d1N1FHVIrt1LwmMC]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

Intact workbench, microscopy, isotope balance, and filament spectrometer. Tests A and C and material tests on personal samples are performed here.

Finding: new filaments incorporate isotopes from LIMEN-9’s nutrients. Risk: missing controls invalidate a conclusion, but the test can be repeated.

11Water Reclamation

@Dir[view|MZx46EPq18yJZQ4t]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|MZx46EPq18yJZQ4t]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

Filter covered in black filaments and plates resembling tooth enamel. A technician can close three valves and drain the circuit, starving the colony of nutrients.

Test D: substrates containing protein accelerate growth. Solution: sterilize for twelve minutes using power from 14; consumes water and raises the environmental risk.

12Morgue

@Dir[view|Oi65WqtfwY4j2GoX]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|Oi65WqtfwY4j2GoX]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

Two identified bodies died in ordinary industrial accidents. A third capsule contains an unfinished face of Dr. Arce, formed on a polymer matrix.

Evidence: links the human fragments to Vesperine’s structure. Limit: does not determine which living person is a copy.

13EIDOLON Archive

@Dir[view|OAjXBIVbfrWgwvGK]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|OAjXBIVbfrWgwvGK]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

A local copy holds procedures on “subjective continuity,” a gag order, and a recording of Arce: “It isn’t the mineral that reproduces memory. It’s whatever secretes it.” The calibrated interferometer is here.

Test B: the sample retains old signals. Definitive clue: NOXUM ordered the colony fed with memories. Playing the contact signal awakens others’ memories in copies, but does not spread infection through audio.

14Reactor

@Dir[view|T1OtJdjfWDQ7KkOd]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|T1OtJdjfWDQ7KkOd]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

Ivo Salcedo hides the fact that he disabled a safety system to gain power. From here, the crew can bypass airlock 01 and power sterilization in 11 and the shuttle in 16.

Extreme decision: removing the regulator (5 min), shutting down heat dissipation (4 min), and forcing maintenance mode (4 min) starts an 18-minute countdown to destruction. The reaction is announced; death is not arbitrary.

15Ducts

@Dir[view|ft0VDRkmNOMeMS2c]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|ft0VDRkmNOMeMS2c]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|swYC10BN9CV0UZE0]{Back to Deck B}

A narrow service route connects 08, 11, 14, and 16. Fresh filaments follow a line of condensation. Section 15-B contains residue from the first replacement, six days ago.

Containment: seal three valves and apply thermal foam for eight minutes. Human evidence: the coveralls belonging to Lía, Ivo’s sister, confirm that she died in a pressure accident.

09Escape Routes

Escape Is Still Possible

Four legitimate ways out. None depends on you “allowing” the ending.
Exit Options · Protecting Evidence and People
Route AAuthorization

WhereAirlock 01

RequirementDecontamination in 02 and signatures from Dalia (Security) and Mara (Medical).

CostThey keep the sample; two frightened people must be persuaded.

Route BBypass

WhereAirlock 01 from 14

RequirementSomeone must operate the reactor panel for 5 min.

CostNOXUM detects it: corporate lockdown. Someone stays in 14.

Route CEVA Collar

Where01 → 17 along the hull

RequirementVaccsuits and tools; 15 min to release the collar.

CostVacuum exposure and a split crew.

Route DFerryman

WhereHangar 16

Requirement6 min of power (battery from 08 or a connection from 14 through 15).

CostOnly three seats: someone gets left behind.

Later Risk

Material isolated without moisture or nutrients cannot cause a replacement in transit; a poorly sealed sample can contaminate a damp system. Survivors may be copies without knowing it: decide using the Absence Log and the evidence obtained.

16*Ferryman* Hangar

@Dir[view|iGzDyhWhXu6Sx3wh]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|iGzDyhWhXu6Sx3wh]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

The auxiliary shuttle Ferryman holds three occupants and carries enough fuel to reach the Widow or a beacon, but needs six minutes of power before launch.

Power: battery from 08 (10 min of work), connection to 14 through Ducts 15 (6 min), or abandon scientific equipment to reduce the load. More than three occupants makes this a dangerous maneuver (Speed Check or another appropriate roll).

17Antenna & Beacon

@Dir[view|MakY3EtPCVHohjjJ]{View the scene} · @Dir[activate|MakY3EtPCVHohjjJ]{Show to everyone} · @Dir[activate|xQpZB94pxUmvgv01]{Back to Deck A}

An EVA walk from airlock 01 leads to a beacon with the original SOS. Unlike the signal in 07, it has no duplicated voice: independent evidence that the alteration happened inside LIMEN-9.

From here, the crew can reach the docking collar and physically unlock it in 15 min with tools. This does not require destroying the station.

10Cast

Eight Survivors

No one acts like “the suspect.” Everyone has human lies you can verify.

Mara Kest

Medical · age 43
Eligible as the first copy

Wants to get three patients out, even if it costs her license. Offers her medical signature in exchange for a compartment to evacuate them. Hides an experimental transfusion; fears another quarantine will kill innocents. Knows everything about 05 and can sign off on departure.

Ivo Salcedo

Reactor · age 35
Eligible as the first copy

Wants to retrieve his sister Lía’s recording from Archive 13. Offers to open the Reactor if they help him. Hides that he bypassed a safety system. Knows how to operate 14, 15, and 16.

Noemí Bas

Comms · age 29
Eligible as the first copy

Wants to copy the original SOS and sell it. Offers the code to 08 if they guarantee her a transmission. Hides the data sale she was arranging. Controls 07 and has the code to 08.

Simón Varek

Archive · age 48
Eligible as the first copy

Wants to recover his wife’s neural archive in 13. Offers to share access permissions if they let him. Hides records he concealed to protect them.

Edda Quill

Inventory · age 24
Eligible as the first copy

Wants to escape before her fraud on manifest CV-11 is exposed. Offers the correct seals. Knows how to decipher seals and explain every cargo movement.

Dalia Voss

Security · age 51
Starts human

Wants to prevent any live sample from leaving. Offers clearance if containment and custody are proven. Hides that she left a technician trapped. Has authority to sign off on departure.

Rafi Ibarra

Mess Hall · age 39
Starts human

Wants to save the person he secretly feeds. Offers schedules and kitchen keys. Has the shift chart and voice recordings in 04.

YARA-7

Maintenance · Android, age 8
Starts intact

Wants to avoid being dismantled. Offers access to 11 and 15 if they promise to get her off the station. Fears NOXUM will scrap her. Has service access and acts even when ordered otherwise.

Roleplaying

A copy can be the most helpful and honest person at the table. Their motivations survive replacement.

11Falsifications

Stations Lie Too

Not every strange thing is the Choir. The station has its own faults, and people have their own fears.

Incidents (1d6)

1d6 Incident
1 A test is positive because of a contaminated container (can be repeated with a control).
2 An automated system predating the accident blocks a route.
3 Dalia aims a weapon at someone over a proven lie, not infection.
4 A latent copy risks their life to help an innocent.
5 Two time logs contradict each other because the terminals’ clocks are out of sync.
6 A valve produces filaments at a measurable rate; someone demands their destruction without investigation.

Pressure Scenes

Everyone gets tested. Dalia proposes sampling the entire crew. One person refuses out of fear or a desire for privacy; this does not mean infection.

A growing sample. In 10, the dry control remains stable while another vial gains mass. The players decide whether to tell NOXUM.

Arce’s Tragedy

Recovering his final audio log does not automatically reveal the Choir. The message reveals a scientist who understands the material’s origin and fears how the corporation will use it: “There is no parent rock. The matrix is alive, and we are feeding it.”

Moral Conflict

If the crew discovers that a copy retains memories and attachments, ask what they consider life. Medical equipment can demonstrate physical changes, not settle once and for all what makes a person. If they choose compassionate containment, let resources and effort make it work. Compelling horror does not demand everyone’s execution.

120-Minute Pacing

0–20 minApproach, contract, first test
20–50 minExplore and cross-check data
50–80 minBiological origin and cover-up
80–105 minCrisis and personal suspicion
105–120 minDecision and epilogue

For a longer session, allow more interactions and experiments; do not extend the clocks.

12The Threat

When the Choir Unfurls

Violence is usually the worst option. Heat, desiccation, and cutting off nutrients work better than trading blows.

Latent Duplicate

Keeps the exact values on their character sheet or NPC profile; gains no additional Skills and does not obey the Choir. A positive material test does not determine intentions: they may ask for help, protect their crewmates, or accept isolation.

Unfurled Form
Copy defending itself
Combat45
Instinct55
Wounds2
AP3

Attack: filament, 2d10 damage at Adjacent Range. If it wounds a PC: Body Save or +1 Imprint.

Seeks to isolate targets and guard matrices. After its first Wound, it breaks line of sight and retreats to 15.

Nest Zero Matrix
Colony in 09
Combat20
Instinct60
Wounds4
AP6

Hazard: pressure from a membrane threatens anyone approaching without protection with 2d10 damage; telegraph the danger and call for a Speed or Body Save.

Never leaves 09. Containment takes three concrete actions: cut off nutrients from 11, close the collectors in 09, and cut power from 14.

Resolution

Use the simplified tracking for contractors for these creatures (Player’s Survival Guide, p. 40): any damage that exceeds their armor counts as one Wound, and they are destroyed upon reaching their maximum Wounds. If a PC takes a Wound from filament, call for a Body Save to avoid contact with active material (+1 Imprint on failure).

Armor (p. 28). Ignore damage below AP; a hit equal to or greater than AP destroys that protection, and the remaining damage goes through. Health and Wounds (pp. 28–29). When a PC’s Health reaches 0, they gain a Wound, roll on the Wounds table for the damage type, and reset their Health to its maximum minus any excess damage. When they reach their maximum Wounds, you make the Death Save (a hidden 1d10). Weapons and cover use their normal values.

Rounds and Violence

The Unfurled Form tries to isolate and guard matrices; it attacks only if someone threatens the nest, its body, or a copy. After taking its first Wound, it breaks line of sight, retreats to 15, and prepares an ambush or a negotiation. It never stays put and fights until its Wounds run out.

Each round lasts about ten seconds: announce the danger, gather decisions, and resolve them simultaneously.

Stress, Fear, Sanity, and Panic

Each failed Stat Check or Save causes 1 Stress (plus the stated consequence); a Critical Failure also triggers a Panic Check. Use Fear for sudden horror, Sanity for contradictions of identity, and Body for physical exposure. Do not turn every strange sound into a roll.

A Copy Is Not Necessarily an Enemy

Only a copy that chooses to unfurl uses the Unfurled Form’s stats. A conscious copy can cooperate in its own study, and the table decides what to do with it.

13Revelation

The Secret Comes Out

At first, Vesperine is extraordinary. By the end, NOXUM knew all along.

Crisis Triggers

The corporation intervenes if it receives a positive sample containing DNA, someone accesses the restricted file in 13, or the reactor loses containment. The characters can uncover the secret before any of these events.

NOXUM uses a euphemism: “Biological resource generating compound V-17.” It will not admit that people were reconstructed unless shown two independent pieces of evidence.

The Document That Proves It

In 13 is the signed authorization: “ORPHEUS Protocol: keep the specimen fed. Human reconstructions are tolerable byproducts.” NOXUM knew the material’s source and put the patent ahead of everyone’s safety.

The Containment Order

Once the secret is undeniable, the company demands that the crew preserve 200 g of viable Vesperine and one reconstructed individual. The team can refuse, negotiate, destroy the evidence, or transmit it to an outside authority.

Three Credible Reactions

Security. Dalia wants to stop material from leaving without inspection. Evidence of NOXUM’s crimes can change her mind.

Researchers. Mara insists on separating evidence from moral judgment; Simón wants to save Arce’s memories.

Corporation. Offers money and logistical support in exchange for silence; then threatens breach-of-contract action. It has neither teleportation nor mind control.

Truth Timeline · The Timing of Each Discovery Sets the Intensity
1Vesperine is extraordinary.
2It grows under biological conditions.
3An organism secretes it.
4It can replicate people.
5NOXUM knew all along. Do not reveal this during the first video call.

14Outcomes

Four Open Endings

Escape is valid even if no one has determined who is a copy.

Cautious Escape

The Widow leaves without active tissue. The group keeps reports on the compound; isolated survivors can be rescued later. NOXUM may claim the patent.

Containment

Closing 09, sterilizing 11, and isolating 15 stops new reconstructions. Existing duplicates do not disappear: the crew decides whether they deserve protection or quarantine. Personal recordings can be preserved.

Destruction

The reactor overloads. There are 18 minutes to evacuate from the actual alarm. Extraordinary knowledge is lost, and the colony is prevented from leaving the station, unless viable material has already been removed.

Negotiation

The Choir may accept an isolated, limited culture environment in exchange for survival, if guaranteed a supply that requires no victims. The corporation has resources, but little reason to honor the agreement. The table decides whom to trust with the future.

Epilogue Questions

Was the discovery published? Who kept the samples? What do you do with someone who has all the memories of a dead person? Whose face appeared in the quarantine camera at the end?

The horror can lie dormant: an isolated strain no longer grows, but the memories, conscious copies, and NOXUM contracts still exist. If the nest is destroyed, the corporation keeps its data. Do not introduce an arbitrary copy in the epilogue: any residue must obey the laws and the logged samples.

What Not to Do

Do not make every NPC a copy. Do not break the exposure laws to heighten tension. Do not block evacuation without plausible routes. Do not demand that the Scientist guess invented terms: listen to their protocols and respond with consistent results.

Warden’s Screen Mothership 1.2 Rules · Player’s Survival Guide

Rolls pp. 18–19

Stat Check or Save: 1d100 (00–99). Succeed by rolling under the score. Add the relevant Skill: Trained +10, Expert +15, Master +20.

90–99 always fails. Each failure gives +1 Stress.

Criticals: any doubles (00, 11, 22… 99). Successful doubles = Critical Success; failed doubles = Critical Failure, which also triggers a Panic Check. 00 is always a Critical Success; 99, always a Critical Failure.

Advantage [+]: roll twice and take the better result. Disadvantage [−]: take the worse. They cancel each other out and apply to any roll (including damage and Panic).

Do not call for rolls for safe, routine scientific work.

Stress p. 20

Starting Minimum Stress 2; maximum 20. Stress above 20 reduces the most relevant Stat or Save by the excess.

Rest: in a safe place, make a Rest Save using your worst Save. Success: reduce Stress by the ones digit. Failure: +1 Stress.

Panic p. 21

Roll 1d20: if you roll over your current Stress, you keep it together. If you roll equal to or under it, look up the result on the Panic Table.

When: after a Critical Failure; when witnessing a crewmate’s death; when witnessing more than one person Panic at once; when encountering a horrific entity for the first time; when all hope is lost; whenever the player chooses.

Rounds pp. 26–27

About 10 seconds. Describe what will happen if no one reacts; everyone declares actions; resolve them simultaneously (rolls, then damage and Wounds).

In one round: move within Close Range and do one thing, or just run to Long Range.

Surprise: Fear Save; anyone who fails cannot react until the next round.

Attacks, Armor, and Wounds pp. 28–29

Attack: Combat Check. Success: roll weapon damage. Failure: the situation gets worse and +1 Stress.

Armor (AP): ignore damage below AP. A hit equal to or above AP destroys the armor; the remaining damage gets through. Anti-Armor weapons ignore and destroy armor.

Health at 0: +1 Wound, roll 1d10 on the Wounds Table for the damage type (Blunt Force, Bleeding, Gunshot, Fire & Explosives, Gore), then reset Health to its maximum minus any excess damage.

Maximum Wounds: Death Save. Roll 1d10 under a cup; reveal it when someone checks vital signs.

Bleeding: 1 damage per round, cumulative; ignores armor.

Cover p. 28
TypeExampleAP
Insignificantfurniture, light doors5
Lightbulkheads, metal furniture10
Heavyairlock doors20 (DR 5)

Anyone firing from cover is exposed until their next turn.

Suits and Oxygen pp. 14–15, 33

Vaccsuit: AP 3, 12 h of air. If punctured, decompression in 1d5 rounds.

Hazard suit: AP 5, 1 h of air; filter, thermal protection, and radiation shielding.

Without oxygen: conscious for 15 s; death follows in 1d5 minutes. Androids do not consume oxygen.

NPCs and Creatures p. 40

They have only Combat, Instinct (for everything else), and Maximum Wounds. They have no Health: each hit that penetrates their armor deals one Wound; at Maximum Wounds, they die.

Trauma Responses character sheet
  • Marine: when they Panic, nearby allies make a Fear Save.
  • Android: nearby allies make Fear Saves with Disadvantage.
  • Scientist: when they fail a Sanity Save, nearby allies gain 1 Stress.
  • Teamster: once per session, Advantage on a Panic Check.

Warden’s Screen EIDOLON Rules

Imprint ch. 03
CauseImprint
10 min without a filter in humid air in 09, 11, or 15+1
Active material in a wound+1
Purging Nest Zero without protection+1

Maximum 3. Brief, avoidable contact: Body Save (success, no effect; failure, +1 Imprint and +1 Stress). Radio and audio do not transmit infection.

Imprint 2 = latent matrix. Not yet a copy.

Replacement all four required at once
  • Imprint 2 or 3.
  • Nearby source: 09, 11, 15, or a copy with moisture present.
  • 4 minutes unwitnessed.
  • Prepared tissue matrix.

Limits: 1 every 30 min; 3 active copies, including the first.

Draw lots: 1 slip for Imprint 2, 2 for Imprint 3. Record name, time, location, and physical evidence.

Testing Individuals

Can distinguish copies: filament spectrometry in 10 (10 min + negative control); interferometry in 13 (2 min motionless + calibration).

Cannot distinguish copies: lab work, hemoglobin, memories, biometrics.

No control: inconclusive. A negative result does not prevent later replacement. Never retroactively invalidate a properly conducted test.

HERMES Tests ch. 04
RoomMinControlReveals
A1012control polymerself-repair
B138reference signalremanence
C1014reference batchlocal isotopes
D1110dry controlorganic dependence

Equipment: 4 controls, 10 capsules, 40 min of battery life; recharge for 15 min in 10 or 14. Roll only under real threat (Intellect + Skill): failure contaminates, delays, or exposes; it never erases the clue.

Clocks advance only when triggered

Recirculation (6, starts at 1): +1/30 min with ventilation, +1 wet area opened, +1 purge. 3 condensation · 5 alarms · 6 widespread exposure.

NOXUM Response (6, starts at 0): +1/60 min, +1 open transmission, +2 biological evidence. 3 preserve samples · 5 retrieval team · 6 remote lockdown.

Life Support (8, starts at 0): +1/30 min without ventilation or reactor, +1 per leak. 4 fatigue · 6 Body Save on exertion · 8 no air.

Adversaries ch. 12
CIWAP
Unfurled Form455523
Nest Zero Matrix206046

Filament: 2d10. Filament Wound: Body Save or +1 Imprint. The matrix never leaves 09; contain it using 11 + 09 + 14.

Investigation Routes

Property: A (10), B (13). Origin: C (10), D (11), manifest in 08. Organism: two of 09, 12, 13. Reconstruction: 12, 13, 15. Cover-up: 08, 13, ORPHEUS.

Every conclusion has at least three paths. Controls and chain of custody matter more than a lucky roll.

Exits ch. 09

A 02 + Dalia’s and Mara’s signatures. B bypass from 14, 5 min. C EVA 01 → 17, 15 min at the collar. D Ferryman in 16: 3 seats, 6 min of power.

Reactor countdown: 5 + 4 + 4 min of operations; then 18 min to evacuate.

Pacing · 120 min

0–20 contract and first test · 20–50 exploration · 50–80 origin and cover-up · 80–105 crisis · 105–120 decision and epilogue.

OPS-V17-01 · Operations Order · Public

Stated ObjectiveUse independent protocols to reproduce four properties of material V-17, designated Vesperine: mechanical integrity, electrical remanence, isotopic provenance, and substrate dependence.
HERMES Resources10 sealed capsules, 4 certified controls, 40 minutes of battery life. Recharge in the laboratory or Reactor: 15 minutes.
Target SampleRecover 200 g in a sealed container. Record the operator, room, time, capsule number, and seal for each sample collected.
Payment20,000 cr for the operation. 5,000 cr for each validated report with a documented chain of custody.
Safety ClauseCrew safety takes priority over material recovery. Any contamination requires a documented chain of custody.

When to hand it out: On docking

CARGA-11A · Logistics · Internal

Declared OriginSurvey of the outer CÍCLOPE-3 belt; batch classified as nonreactive silicate sediment.
Mass and Route10 kg. Barge IMAGO 5 → LIMEN-9 / Storage 08. Custodian: Edda Quill.
CertificationNo detectable metabolism. Exempt from biological quarantine. Certificate issued before physical receipt of the batch.
Inventory NoteNew containers accumulate more material than was removed from the initial sample. The difference is not logged as incoming cargo.

Run a mass balance. — E. Q.

When to hand it out: When found in 08

LAB-HRM-03 · HERMES · Laboratory · Public · Form

Sample and OperatorOperator: ____________________ Time: ________
Room: ________ Capsule No.: ______ Seal: ________
ControlsNegative control: ____________________
Positive control: ____________________
Tests☐ A · Integrity · 12 min ☐ valid control
☐ B · Remanence · 8 min ☐ valid control
☐ C · Isotopes · 14 min ☐ valid control
☐ D · Nutrients · 10 min ☐ valid control
NotesHypothesis: ______________________________________
Observed result: ____________________________
Possible contamination: ________________________

A test without a control may offer a lead, but it does not prove a hypothesis.

When to hand it out: On docking (photocopiable)

LAB-HRM-04 · HERMES · Results · Internal

Test A · IntegrityA cut sheet recovers almost all its original strength. The control polymer remains cut. The sterilized sample recovers more slowly.
Test B · RemanenceAfter power is removed, three staggered pulses are detected that do not belong to the current stimulus. The pattern partially matches a station file.
Limited InferenceThe sample reorganizes itself and retains information. Neither result establishes that the material is conscious or determines its origin.

When to hand it out: After completing A and B

LAB-HRM-05 · Analysis · Tracers · Internal

Test C · ProvenanceRecent deposits incorporate isotopic signatures from LIMEN-9’s recirculated water and organic medium. They do not come solely from batch CV-11.
Test D · MediaRelative growth: organic medium 195%, saline solution 47%, dry control 5%. Only the organic medium sustains accelerated growth.
Preliminary ConclusionA local synthesis or secretion process requires resources from the facility. The geological manifest does not account for all the material observed.

When to hand it out: After completing C and D

SEG-Q-08 · Security · Quarantine · Internal

CircuitsIsolate ventilation and water circuits between Decks A and B; reopen only after diagnostic clearance.
PersonnelAll evacuations require a medical examination and Security clearance, or a manual override of exit controls.
MaterialTransport all V-17 in numbered, sealed containers. Do not remove open or wet samples.
ExceptionsEvacuation of injured personnel may be authorized with signatures from medical staff and Security.

It’s not a disease. I don’t know what it is. Don’t let anything that grows get out. — D. V.

When to hand it out: When found in 02 or 06

COM-07/17 · Telemetry · Comms · Internal

Channel 07 · Local Network · 02:14:03“We’re still here… the laboratory… don’t send…” The waveform shows a second, overlapping voice offset by 0.27 s.
Channel 17 · External Beacon · 02:14:03“We’re still here… the laboratory… don’t send…” No second voice. The original signal is identical until it enters the repeater.
Open HypothesesProcessing error, file modification, or interference by the connected substrate. The voice does not spread infection.

When to hand it out: After comparing 07 and 17

MED-12-03 · Forensic Medicine · Internal

Anatomical SamplePartially formed human tissue on a black matrix, with no signs of transplantation or surgery. Structural filaments match V-17.
Incomplete IdentificationPartial match with Gael Arce; neither identity nor state of consciousness is certified.
LimitationsThis report confirms the fabrication of tissue consistent with human tissue. It does not, on its own, prove that a survivor is a copy.

When to hand it out: When found in 12

I+D-ORF-00 · Restricted Directorate · Confidential
